source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul pentru 22 octombrie — «Sfânta Muceniță Teodota»

attestations.note: doxologia.ro prints no separate life for her: the page under her name carries the same four sentences that stand under each of the four women's names, which are the synaxarion notice of Alexander the bishop. The epithet “of Adrianople” is taken from the calendar's own line for Glyceria, «Sfânta Muceniță Gligheria din Adrianopol», the only one of the four whose line names the city; the other three lines give the bare name.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 22ης Οκτωβρίου — «Άγιοι Αλέξανδρος ο Επίσκοπος, Ηράκλειος, Άννα, Ελισάβετ, Θεοδότη και Γλυκερία»

attestations.note: The life page `https://www.saint.gr/2778/saint.aspx` heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 22 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps for the Romanian church, and the company is the same: a bishop Alexander, a soldier Heraclius who believed on seeing him tortured, and four women — Theodote, Glyceria, Anna and Elizabeth — whom Alexander drew to the faith by a wonder and who were beheaded before him. **The Greek page names no city**, so nothing here confirms or contradicts the Adrianople of the folder's English name; it gives no year, no emperor and no see, so no `dates` object is proposed and no coordinate. Alexander and Heraclius are drafted as new folders in batch el-10-22. No hymn is printed for any of the six. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (24 September 2026).
